semantic_contract: 0x00c0c130 is a single-byte flag accessor on a polymorphic simulator object. Its entire behaviour is: load the byte at receiver + 0xbb1 into AL and return. It reads no other field, writes no memory, touches no global, calls nothing, cannot fail and has no branch. The value is forwarded raw rather than normalised, so a byte of 0xff returns as 0xff, and only AL is defined on exit. The two inspected consumers both treat it as a boolean gate on the code immediately following the call: in 0x00c03950 a set flag makes the caller return 0 without reading [EBX + 0xc0], and in the 0x00c03b00 region a set flag jumps out of a float-comparison sequence. The receiver is the same object whose collection 0x00c0c080 searches and whose fields at +0xa60, +0xb34, +0xb74, +0xbb0, +0xe80 and +0xe84 the neighbouring accessors in 0x00c0c0d0..0x00c0c1c0 read and write, so +0xbb0 and +0xbb1 are two independent one-byte states sitting side by side in a larger per-object state block. What the flag means is not established by any evidence in this batch.
classification_rationale: Both instructions, the exact bytes, the field offset, the byte width, the raw-value semantics, the undefined upper bits of EAX, the ABI, the absence of any write and the absence of any branch are read directly from the disassembly and from a live memory read, and the gating behaviour is corroborated by two inspected callers in the same code region. STRONG_SEMANTIC is withheld for two named bounds. First, the owning class is not established: no MSVC RTTI exists, a positive-controlled .rdata/.data scan found no vtable entry for 0x00c0c130 or its sibling 0x00c0c120, and no ModAPI header declares a class with byte fields at +0xbb0 and +0xbb1. Second, and more materially, the meaning of the flag is not established: the field is only ever read here and by its sibling, no writer of +0xbb1 was located, and the two consumers gate unrelated work (a dword read at +0xc0 in one, a float comparison in the other) without agreeing on a subject. The bound is the flag's semantics and the class identity; the load-and-return behaviour carries no residual uncertainty.
semantic_findings: 0x00c0c130 returns one byte from receiver +0xbb1 and does nothing else; the whole contract is a field read.
The value is raw, not a normalised boolean: MOV AL rather than MOV EAX, and no TEST or AND against 1.
Only AL is defined on exit, so the function's C++ signature must return a byte-sized type; an int-returning declaration would read eight undefined bits.

The immediately adjacent sibling 0x00c0c120 has the identical seven-byte shape one byte lower, so +0xbb0 and +0xbb1 are a pair of independent byte flags rather than a byte and its high half of anything.
Both inspected callers branch on the result immediately after the call, so the flag is a gate on the following work rather than a value that is consumed arithmetically.
The flag is a per-instance state, not a global: it is read through ECX, and 0x00c03950 and the 0x00c03b00 region pass two different receivers.
Neither 0x00c0c130 nor 0x00c0c120 is a vtable entry, so this accessor is a free function over a concrete class and no SDK interface name applies.

The receiver is a large stateful object: the same instance also carries a float source at +0xa60, a dword compared against 1 at +0xb34, a dword at +0xb74, a pointer with two byte flags at +0xe84, and a searchable collection reached through vtable slots +0xb0 and +0xb4.
